ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $CE$ is the bisector of the exterior angle $\angle ACD$ of $\triangle ABC$. If $\angle B = 45^\circ$ and $\angle ACE = 65^\circ$, then what is the measure of $\angle A$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $CE$ is the bisector of $\angle ACD$ and $\angle ACE=65^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle ACD=130^\circ$.\\
Since $\angle ACD$ is an exterior angle of $\triangle ABC$,\\
we have $\angle ACD=\angle A + \angle B$.\\
Given that $\angle B=45^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle A=\boxed{85^\circ}$.

method.method_draft: First describe the figure: triangle ABC has B, C, D on one straight horizontal line with D to the right of C, and a ray CE goes upward-right outside the triangle; the marked exterior angle at C is between CA and CD and is split by CE. Read from the text that CE bisects exterior angle ACD, angle B is 45°, and angle ACE is 65°. Use the angle-bisector rule to make exterior angle ACD = 2·65° = 130°.
